# Pahīnavāra (Ya 7.2.5)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pahīnavāra* ("Section on What Is Abandoned") is a leaf division within the *Anusayayamaka*, the seventh major book of the *Yamaka* in the Abhidhammapiṭaka [SuttaCentral; Nyanatiloka 1938]. In the analytical architecture of the *Anusayayamaka*, it constitutes the fifth section of the second chapter (treating the *anusayas* or latent defilements / biases), following the *Anusayavāra*, *Sānusayavāra*, *Pajahanavāra*, and *Pariññāvāra*, and preceding the *Uppajjanavāra* and *Dhātuvāra* [Nyanatiloka 1938]. Like the rest of the work, it applies the distinctive Yamaka method of paired, logically exhaustive interrogations (applied here to which latent defilements are abandoned, by what stages or paths, and for which individuals) [Nyanatiloka 1938; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation of the text [SuttaCentral].
No direct canonical parallels in other Buddhist traditions are curated by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. However, computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus reveals over 23,000 Pali-internal matches across 67 texts, reflecting the formulaic structural reuse throughout the Abhidhamma [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual partners are adjacent divisions of the *Anusayayamaka*, principally the *Anusayavāra* (Ya 7.2.1), *Sānusayavāra* (Ya 7.2.2), *Pariññāvāra* (Ya 7.2.4), and *Uppajjanavāra* (Ya 7.2.6), as well as the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* [DharmaNexus]. The section is commented upon in the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and further glossed in the *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* and *Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects substantial phrase-sharing with the *Ñāṇakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* and the *Sattakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* [DharmaNexus]. In non-Pali corpora, machine alignments highlight conceptual and terminological parallels regarding the abandonment of defilements in Sanskrit and Tibetan scholastic treatises, including Sthiramati's *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā*, Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya* and its *Vyākhyā*, the *Karmaprajñapti*, and the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* [DharmaNexus].
